title: Silver found at Potosí; mined by forced mita labour
summary: Diego Huallpa, an Indigenous prospector, is traditionally credited with finding the Cerro Rico's silver in 1545. Under the mita, about 13,000 Indigenous men a year were conscripted; many died from falls, accidents, harsh conditions and mercury poisoning.
why: Its silver flooded world trade, from Spain to China.

notes.problem: Passive "was found" erased the Indigenous prospector traditionally credited; "forced labour" did not name the mita, its scale or the deaths.
